equivalents.note: The line has rnal 'byor without the feminine ma, probably shortened for the metre (Munidatta's paraphrase in cp.04.m3 has bdag med rnal 'byor ma), so read alone it could mean 'yogi' or 'yoga'.
lde mig ordinarily means 'key', so with lde kyog, 'hooked key', beside it the Tibetan line may name two keys rather than a key and a lock.

Where the Sanskrit nirābhāsīkṛtya means 'having made free of appearance', the Tibetan has shin du gsal snang du byas pa, 'made into a very clear appearance', as if it read nirbhāsa, 'shining forth', or took nir- as intensive: the opposite sense.
The Tibetan splits the compound nirātmayoginī into two words, rnal 'byor ma bdag med ma, 'the yoginī, Nairātmā'.
For gurusampradāyāt, 'from the guru's lineage', the Tibetan has bla ma'i drin las, 'through the guru's kindness'.

The Tibetan has 'joy of variety' where the Sanskrit has viramānanda, 'joy of cessation'; sna tshogs normally renders vicitra, so its manuscript may have read another word, and the same substitution recurs in cp.04.m5.

equivalents.wylie: nag po spyod pa pa'i zhabs
equivalents.note: Nag po spyod pa, 'Black Conduct', takes the name as Kṛṣṇa-caryā rather than Kṛṣṇa-ācārya, 'master Kṛṣṇa'; the doubled pa here (not in cp.04.m5) may be a slip.
The honorific thugs, as in the series sku, gsung, thugs rdo rje that renders kāyavajra, vāgvajra, cittavajra.
lde mig yang dag par sbyor bar byed pa, 'properly joining the lde mig', renders tālasampuṭīkaraṇa, 'sealing the lock shut', so the comment also uses lde mig for tāla.
As in cp.04.m3, the Tibetan has 'variety joy' for viramānanda in viramānandāvadhūtikā.

The Tibetan takes sampradāya in its root sense of 'handing over' (de rnams rab tu byin pa las gzhan, 'other than those who have been fully given it'), not as 'lineage', for sampradāyabahirmukha, 'turned away from the lineage'.

questions: yogini in cp.04.1a: the Tibetan line (ka mgo non la yan lag 'khyud la byin) has no word for the vocative joini; the yoginī is not named until 2a (rnal 'byor) and 3a (rnal 'byor ma), so there is nothing to match.

vira in cp.04.5a: the Tibetan line (guN+Da rI bdag kun+Da re pa smras) has no word for bīrā, 'hero'; the suffix pa in kun+Da re pa, 'one of kundura', may stand in for it. Munidatta's comment (cp.04.m6) has dpa' bo, already matched.

carya in cp.04.m1: the Tibetan has dpal he ru ka'i rtogs pa, 'understanding of Śrī Heruka', with no spyod pa for -caryā- in śrīherukacaryāvagamena; either its manuscript lacked the word or the translators dropped it.
tx-hevajra in cp.04.m3: the Tibetan leaves out 'tathā ca śrīhevajre' and gives the verse (skal med DiN+Di ma ru brjod...) with no named source, so there is no Tibetan title to match.
